answer_1.quote: Our primary goal is to train a high-performing multilingual student model S. Given a set of input prompts P = {p i } N i=1 , we generate a corresponding set of completions C = {c i } N i=1 using a pool of potential teacher models T = {T j } M j=1 . These prompt-completion pairs (p i , c i ) will then be used to fine-tune S.
answer_1.outputs: Generated completions (synthetic data) for training student models

answer_2.quote: We analyze the impact of instruction fine-tuning (IFT) with multilingual arbitration on text verbosity, readability, and lexical diversity. Reward-based routing increases token count by 14.1%, while learned routing leads to a 68.4% increase compared to both single-teacher and random routing baselines. Lexical diversity also improves: reward-based routing achieves a 6% gain, and learned routing 4.2%, relative to single teachers, with 13.4% and 11.5% gains over random routing, respectively.
